reason: The test suite fails; tests that directly enforce the core requirements (SPEC-1/R-8, SPEC-3/R-10, SPEC-7/R-9, SPEC-9/R-12) all fail, and the change to `cycle-orchestrator.sh` introduces regressions in cycle-reset behavior that break at least four previously-passing test files.

unmet: R-1/R-2/R-3/R-8 (A resume trusts every stage that already ran; outputs rehydrated; run picks up at interrupted stage; stage k dispatched): `tests/integration/resume-rehydrate-test.sh` fails on three SPEC-1 assertions — "intake emits no stage.start (complete stage skipped)" for all three resume entry paths — meaning the dispatch loop is still dispatching completed stages on resume rather than skipping them.

R-4/R-10 (--from-stage rehydrates every earlier stage and dispatches s first): `tests/integration/from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh` fails on "[#1805/SPEC-3] intake emits no stage.start when skipped via --from-stage", meaning intake is still being dispatched rather than skipped.

R-9 (loop resume restores iteration count, not reset): `tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh` fails on "[#1805/SPEC-7] no cycle.iteration.complete for iter=1 (iter-1 was already done before resume)", meaning the iteration-state restore on resume does not work correctly.

R-12 (every resume entry path finds state in runs/<run_id>/ and behaves as R1): `tests/integration/resume-entry-points-test.sh` fails; the cyclic-stage dispatch assertion is unmet (expected >0, got: 0), and the SPEC-1 path-2 and path-3 assertions in `resume-rehydrate-test.sh` also fail.

R-15 (tests for R1–R5 use a cycle): `tests/integration/resume-entry-points-test.sh` SPEC-13 fails — the assertion that the cycled stage dispatched (got: 0) means the cyclic pipeline did not run through a cycle in that test.

R-13/R-14 (no prior state behaves as today; new run never skips): The change to `cycle-orchestrator.sh` reads `current_iter` from persisted state unconditionally for every cycle entry — not only on resume — causing inner cycles in nested loop structures to start at iter=2 instead of resetting to iter=1. This breaks `cycle-inner-iter-resets-per-outer-iter-test.sh`, `nested-loop-rounds-test.sh`, `nested-loop-rounds-build-test.sh`, and `cycle-member-dispatch-events-test.sh`; the guard for "a new run behaves as today" is therefore violated.
